AI Gateway now supports team-wide Zero Data Retention (ZDR).

Building safely with multiple AI models means wrestling with fragmented data policies, per-provider negotiations, and the hope that developers do not use non-complaint providers.

AI Gateway changes this with team-wide ZDR.

Gateway ensures your data requirements are automatically met by only routing to providers where we have negotiated ZDR agreements.

Instead of managing policies provider by provider, you get one unified data policy across Claude, GPT, Gemini, and many more providers.

Toggle it on in your dashboard, and all requests will route safely without touching any code:
  • Team-wide ZDR
  • Per-request controls
  • Disallow prompt training

Move compliance to the gateway so your team can keep shipping ↓

recent_posts.title: Vercel Flags now supports JSON values
recent_posts.summary: Vercel Flags now supports JSON values in addition to boolean, string, and number types. This lets developers consolidate multiple related feature flags into a single structured flag. A practical use case is A/B testing AI model configurations — instead of managing separate flags for model ID, temperature, and max tokens, you can store the full configuration object as a single flag variant. This also enables progressive traffic routing and quick model switching when a provider has issues.

recent_posts.title: Auto-add Git committers to your team
recent_posts.summary: Vercel Pro teams can now configure how Git committers to private repositories are added to their team. Two options are available: Auto Approval, where non-team committers with Vercel accounts are instantly added and their deployments proceed immediately (counting toward team seats at Pro pricing), and Manual Approval, where deployments are blocked until an owner reviews and approves the new member. The setting is configurable in team collaboration settings.

recent_posts.title: Secure Marketplace credentials with Production-only access
recent_posts.summary: Vercel now allows native integration resources to be restricted to Production-only access. Enabling this setting converts credentials to sensitive environment variables (unreadable from dashboard or CLI), removes Development and Preview connections, and blocks new non-production connections. Reverting requires Owner permissions and may trigger an MFA challenge.

recent_posts.title: Query observability metrics using the Vercel CLI
recent_posts.summary: Vercel has added a new `vercel metrics` command to the Vercel CLI, now in public beta for teams with Observability Plus. It allows developers to query observability data (performance, reliability, security) for any Vercel team or project programmatically. Coding agents can also use this command to analyze and debug applications on Vercel.

recent_posts.title: Introducing deepsec: The security harness for finding vulnerabilities in your codebase
recent_posts.summary: Vercel is open sourcing deepsec, an AI-powered security scanning tool that uses coding agents (Claude Opus and GPT) to find vulnerabilities in large codebases. It runs locally or scales to 1,000+ concurrent Vercel Sandboxes for parallel execution. The workflow includes static regex scanning, agent-based investigation, revalidation to reduce false positives (reported at 10-20%), contributor enrichment via git metadata, and exportable findings. It supports a plugin system for custom scanners tuned to specific auth models or data layers. No special 'cyber' AI models are required — standard Claude and Codex subscriptions work out of the box.

recent_posts.title: Grok 4.3 on AI Gateway
recent_posts.summary: Grok 4.3 is now available on Vercel's AI Gateway. The model features a December 2025 knowledge cutoff and a 1M token context window. It can be accessed by setting the model to `xai/grok-4.3` in the AI SDK. Vercel AI Gateway provides a unified API for model access, usage tracking, cost monitoring, retries, failover, and observability — with no markup and no separate provider account required.

recent_posts.title: Custom tags available in beta on Vercel Sandbox
recent_posts.summary: Vercel Sandbox now supports custom tags in open beta, allowing teams to organize, filter, and manage sandboxes at scale. Each sandbox supports up to five key-value tags that can be set at creation or updated later. Tags enable use cases like separating staging from production environments, attributing usage to specific teams, isolating sandboxes per customer in multi-tenant platforms, and tracking AI agent execution environments. Filtering sandboxes by tag is supported via the SDK for dashboards, cleanup scripts, and routing logic. The feature requires upgrading to the beta SDK and CLI packages.

recent_posts.title: Vercel now supports Pro plan in Stripe Projects
recent_posts.summary: Vercel now supports Pro plan provisioning and upgrades directly from Stripe Projects using shared payment tokens (SPTs). Developers and agents can manage Vercel plan changes programmatically via the Stripe CLI without switching between dashboards. The feature supports both upgrade and downgrade flows and builds on the earlier Stripe Projects developer preview. Getting started requires installing the Stripe projects plugin and running a single CLI command.

recent_posts.title: Native Deployment Checks are now available
recent_posts.summary: Vercel has launched Native Deployment Checks, allowing teams to run lint and typecheck scripts on every deployment in parallel with the build. Configured via project Build and Deployment settings, Vercel executes the matching script from package.json and skips if none exists. Checks can be marked as required to block production deployments until they pass, and can be scoped to specific environments. When a check fails on a pull request, Vercel Agent automatically investigates and suggests a fix.

recent_posts.title: Hobby projects now default to 30-day deployment retention
recent_posts.summary: Vercel is capping deployment retention for Hobby plan users at 30 days starting April 29th. Deployments older than 30 days will be automatically deleted, with exceptions for the 10 most recent production deployments and any aliased deployments, which are always preserved. Pro and Enterprise plans are unaffected.
